# write_entry { #crossrepo.manifest.write_entry }

```python
crossrepo.manifest.write_entry(text, key, description)
```

Put one file into a manifest, leaving the rest of it alone.

Publishing is naming a file, so this is the act of publishing one. An entry
already there has its description rewritten and keeps whatever else it
carries: a stamp belongs to the file, not to the sentence describing it, and
a re-description should not send the content back to be read again.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**text**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Content of the manifest. An empty string starts one.

<code>[**key**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Key to write, as a path relative to the manifest or, with a leading ``/``, from the root of the repository.

<code>[**description**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   What the file holds.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The manifest with the entry written.

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
write_entry("files:\n  a.csv: one\n", "b.csv", "another")
# 'files:\n  a.csv: one\n  b.csv: another\n'
```
